headline: Stocks fell for a fourth straight day (S&P 500 -1.03% to 7,341, its lowest close since late July; Dow -1.64%) with the 10-year at 5.11% and a December Fed hike nearly priced, but Nvidia beat and guided to about $130B and rose after hours.
regime: Hiking regime: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00% after a 10-2 hold in October, and a 25bp December hike is nearly fully priced (95-96% per KuCoin Nov 18; 100% per futures on Nov 12). The 10-year closed at 5.11%, the VIX was about 25.5 before the Nov 17 open and the FOMC minutes arrive today.

lean.t: Nvidia beat vs a falling tape
lean.why: Nvidia rose about 4.8% after hours, but the S&P has lost four days in a row and the FOMC minutes plus Target, Lowe's, TJX and Palo Alto (after the close) all land today.
A December hike is nearly priced, the 10-year is above 5% and the VIX is about 25; PCE (Nov 25) and the Dec 8-9 FOMC are ahead.
Nvidia guides to about $130B next quarter, but a hiking Fed and software worries (Salesforce -9.5%) weigh on valuations.

news.head: Nvidia beats and guides to about $130B; shares rise after hours
news.srcN: StockTitan, Nov 17 (updated 8:30 PM ET); Motley Fool/Yahoo, Nov 17
news.mean: Fiscal Q3 revenue was $115.8B (+103%), net income $64.9B and data center revenue $107.6B; Q4 guidance is about $130B plus or minus 3%. The stock closed $155.46 (-0.44%) and was up 4.81% (about $162.94) at 7:59 PM ET; Motley Fool cited a smaller early gain of about 1.3%.
react: Up 7.5% after hours on a Marvell patent deal
Direction at the open depends on whether the gain holds
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a strong print from the AI-chip leader tends to lift the group at the open, but gains often fade if the broader market is falling.
news.today: Watch whether the after-hours gain holds after Nov 17's fourth straight S&P 500 loss.
news.later: Investors may weigh the ~$130B guide against rate risk with the 10-year above 5%.

news.head: S&P 500 posts a fourth straight loss, lowest close since late July
news.srcN: Motley Fool, Nov 17; StockTitan citing CNBC, Nov 17
news.mean: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,341, the Dow 1.64% to 50,759 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.74% to 24,328 (it was down about 2.1% intraday, its lowest level since April, per CNBC via StockTitan). The IWM small-cap fund fell 1.43%. The VIX was 25.46 before the open.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: streaks of losses into a major earnings report often end with a sharp relief or follow-through move; the direction is not predictable.
news.today: Expect wide swings around Nvidia's reaction, FOMC minutes and retail earnings.
news.later: Investors may note the S&P is at its lowest close since late July while the Fed is expected to hike.

news.head: Salesforce drops 9.5% as software sells off on AI-replacement fears
news.mean: Salesforce fell 9.45% to $194.52 as software shares sold off on security concerns and fears that AI will replace software.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sector-wide software selloffs on a narrative can overshoot or extend; earnings reports are what usually settle them.
news.today: Palo Alto Networks reports after the close Nov 18 and may move the cyber and software group.
news.later: Investors may watch whether software earnings back up or contradict the AI-replacement worry.

news.head: December hike odds sit near a lock; FOMC minutes due today
news.srcN: KuCoin, Nov 18; Motley Fool, Nov 16; Investing.com, Nov 10
news.mean: KuCoin (Nov 18) cites 95-96% for a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting and about 5% for 50bp; Motley Fool (Nov 16) cited 100% per fed funds futures as of Nov 12, and Investing.com showed 88.8% on Nov 10. The target is 3.75-4.00% after a 10-2 hold in October (Cook and Hammack favored a hike). KuCoin also shows traders at 67% for a January hike.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: when a hike is already fully priced, the minutes and the guidance on pace matter more than the decision itself.
news.today: Watch the minutes for the split between a 25bp and a 50bp move.
news.later: Investors may plan for a higher-for-longer path, with KuCoin showing at least three hikes priced by end-2027.

news.head: Fed officials split on pace: Waller floats 50bp, Williams sees no major increase
news.mean: Waller said on Nov 10 a 50bp hike should be considered in December if inflation stays high; Musalem sees several more hikes before spring; Logan may want to move faster; Williams said Nov 17 conditions do not support a major increase; Bowman favors smaller, gradual steps; Chair Warsh gave no clear December signal on Nov 16.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a divided committee tends to raise rate volatility around data releases.
news.today: Today's minutes can reveal how many members wanted a larger move.
news.later: Investors may weigh the path of rates into 2027.

news.head: 10-year yield 5.11% on Nov 17 after a hot CPI week
news.mean: The 10-year closed at 5.11%, down 3 basis points. Investing.com's Nov 10 page showed the 30-year at 5.447% and 5-year at 4.915% (undated snapshot). October CPI on Nov 10 was hotter than expected at +0.4% headline and +0.3% core per KuCoin.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: yields above 5% have tended to cap valuations for long-duration growth.
news.today: A move below 5% would be notable.
news.later: Investors may weigh bonds at 5%+ against stock valuations.

news.head: Gold near $3,849, crude in the mid-$80s
news.srcN: Motley Fool, Nov 17; Investing.com via Yahoo, Nov 17
news.mean: Gold settled at $3,849.20 (-0.18%) per Motley Fool, while pre-open tickers showed $3,780 to $3,786 (timing not stated). December crude was about $84.5-84.7 before the open (-1.78%).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold tends to struggle when real yields rise.
news.today: Gold quotes differ by source and time; check the contract month.
news.later: Investors may view gold as a hedge but rate-sensitive.

news.head: October retail sales +0.2%, industrial production -0.4%
news.srcN: StockTitan citing Census, Fed and BLS, Nov 17
news.mean: Retail sales rose 0.2% to $748.2B after +0.8% in September; industrial production fell 0.4% (utilities -4.3%) after +0.7%; import prices rose 1.1%.
react: Import prices add to inflation concern
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a soft retail print with hot import prices keeps the stagflation debate alive.
news.today: Watch Target, Lowe's and TJX for consumer color.
news.later: Investors may follow the PCE inflation data on Nov 25.

news.head: Home Depot beats on sales, names new CEO
news.srcN: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, Nov 17; StockTitan, Nov 17
news.mean: Q3 sales were $43.4B (+4.9%) versus about $42.8B expected; FY2026 sales growth guidance is about 4.5%; Richard McPhail becomes CEO Nov 23. Shares closed -2.45%. Housing starts print today at 8:30 ET.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: housing-related stocks tend to track mortgage rates more than single earnings beats.
news.today: Lowe's call at 9:00 AM ET and housing starts at 8:30 AM ET are the next reads.
news.later: Investors may watch mortgage rates (last survey on file 7.18%).

news.head: UnitedHealth falls 5.4% on Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud proposals
news.mean: UnitedHealth fell 5.42% on anti-fraud proposals for Medicare and Medicaid.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy headlines hit insurers fast, and details often matter more than the first reaction.
news.today: Watch for follow-up detail on the proposals.
news.later: Investors may track how any rules would affect reimbursement.

news.head: Nvidia to stop selling chips to data centers renting most GPUs to Chinese firms
news.srcN: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, Nov 17 (citing CNBC)
news.mean: Nvidia told customers it will stop selling to data center operators that rent more than half their GPUs to Chinese companies; the premarket article also says Nvidia has lost about $410B in value since CEO Jensen Huang resigned and that its board created a national security and export control committee (StockTitan).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: export-control news can change addressable markets for chip suppliers.
news.later: Investors may weigh export rules as a structural risk.

news.head: JD.com and Tencent Music report; Red Cat pulls its revenue target
news.srcN: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, Nov 17; StockTitan, Nov 17
news.mean: JD.com Q3 revenue was RMB309.6B versus 311.48B expected (stock -7.66%); Tencent Music revenue was RMB8.94B versus 9.14B expected (stock +6.64%); Red Cat fell 31.73% after withdrawing its 2026 revenue target.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: earnings misses at smaller names tend to produce outsized one-day moves.
news.today: Watch for follow-through in China ADRs.
news.later: Investors may separate company-specific from macro drivers.

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
